question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $Z,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $11\,|\,(x-y).$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $-6?$

I. $[5]$

II. $[-17]$

III. $[-8]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $-6\in [x]$ if $-6∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}11\,|\,(-6-x).\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $-6\in [5]$ because $11\,|\,(-6-5)\,✓$

- $-6\in [-17]$ because $11\,|\,(-6+17)\,✓$

- $-6\notin [-8]$ because $11∤(-6+8)\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
